newsitem.title: UK: Coffee talks end, rules of origin discussed.
newsitem.headline: Coffee talks end, rules of origin discussed.

text.p: Coffee producers and consumers were on Friday wrapping-up talks of the International Coffee Organization with a debate over proposed European Union changes to rules of coffee origin and elections of the ICO Board.
ICO delegates on Friday said EU members have proposed changes to the rules of coffee origin which are now being debated by the Brussels-based World Customs Organization (WCO).

The WCO's Committee of Rules of Origin is considering the proposals to label coffee processed beyond a certain degree in any given EU importing country as originating there and not in the growing country, said ICO delegates.
ICO producer delegates were on Friday upset by the proposals and wary of them being implemented.
"We are very concerned about the proposed changes. We believe the origin of coffee is where it is produced," an ICO producer delegate told Reuters on Friday.
Officials from the WCO's Committe of Rules of Origin were not available for comment on Friday.
ICO producers were said to be drafting a response to the proposed EU changes.
"Changing the rules of origin would destroy all the added value that producers at origin give to the coffee bean," said another ICO producer delegate.
In other business, the ICO this week approved the draft administrative budget for 1996/97 and a project to develop gourmet coffee potential.
The gourmet project will enable five coffee-producers, including three African ones, to implement sustainable gourmet quality development and marketing strategies.

Another project, backed by the ICO, which aims to control the spread of coffee berry borer has been approved by the Fund's Consultative Committee and delegates said it was poised to be approved by the Fund's Executive Board.

And delegates said on Friday they were informed that a study of marketing and trading policies and systems in selected coffee-producing countries had also been approved by the UN's Common Fund's Executive Board.

The ICO was also debating proposed changes to the way it presents its coffee export statistics when origins export two or more types of coffee and the robusta-arabica weighting of its ICA composite indicator.
"The ICO's indicator price dates back to 1979. It is time it was revised," said one ICO European consumer delegate.
The ICO Council's final piece of work on Friday was to elect a new chairman and new Board officials, said delegates.
